THOUGHT: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman with vaginal bleeding and a thickened endometrial stripe on ultrasound, and endometrial biopsy showing well-differentiated adenocarcinoma, indicates endometrial carcinoma. The concurrent palpable left adnexal mass and elevated inhibin B point to an ovarian sex-cord stromal tumor, specifically an adult granulosa cell tumor, which secretes estrogen. Excess estrogen from a granulosa cell tumor commonly causes endometrial hyperplasia and can lead to endometrial (often endometrioid) adenocarcinoma in postmenopausal women. The non-tender adnexal mass, elevated inhibin B (a granulosa cell tumor marker), and the presence of endometrial cancer together make an estrogen-producing granulosa cell tumor with secondary endometrial carcinoma the most likely unifying diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Adult granulosa cell tumor of the ovary causing estrogen excess with secondary well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma.
